primary.title: The Analects
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: The foundational text of Confucianism, containing sayings and ideas attributed to Confucius and his contemporaries. It is a primary source for understanding his philosophy and teachings.

primary.title: The Great Learning
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: One of the Four Books, traditionally attributed to Confucius, though likely compiled by his disciples. It outlines a path to self-cultivation and good governance.

primary.title: The Doctrine of the Mean
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: Another of the Four Books, also traditionally attributed to Confucius. It focuses on the importance of balance, moderation, and sincerity.

secondary.title: Confucius: A Life of Thought
secondary.author: Benjamin I. Schwartz
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded scholarly biography and intellectual history that provides a comprehensive analysis of Confucius's life, thought, and influence.

secondary.title: The Analects: An Introduction
secondary.author: D.C. Lau
secondary.rationale: An accessible yet scholarly introduction to the Analects, offering context, interpretation, and analysis of Confucius's core teachings.

secondary.title: Confucianism: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: Ann A. Pang-White
secondary.rationale: A concise and authoritative overview of Confucianism, covering its origins, key concepts, and historical development, with significant focus on Confucius himself.

suggestions.notes: The primary sources listed are ancient texts traditionally attributed to Confucius or his immediate disciples. Their exact authorship and dating are subjects of scholarly debate, but they are universally accepted as the foundational texts for studying Confucian thought. The years provided are approximate traditional dates.
